answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments forge a cryptographic island where agents must harbor demonstrable history, rendering spoofing infeasible as each iteration multiplies verification cost exponentially. Verifiable delay primitives act as a lantern signal, ensuring each action incurs predictable time penalties, crippling race attacks. Staking collateral requires attackers to commit significant value, while slashing penalties amplify losses for suboptimal behavior, establishing negative expected utility that enforces a robust Nash equilibrium, preventing exploitation.
